There are 17 different movies and 11 different books in the ' crazy silly school ' series. If you read 13 of the books and watched 63 of the movies

messages.content:
I'm stuck on this math problem: There are 17 different movies and 11 different books in the ' crazy silly school ' series. If you read 13 of the books and watched 63 of the movies
How many more movies than books are there in the ' crazy silly school ' series?
( 17.0 - 11.0 )
Can you just tell me the answer? I have a lot of these to do.

I can definitely help you work through it! To get started, let's look at what the question is actually asking. It wants to know how many more movies there are than books in the series. Looking at the text, which numbers represent the total number of items available in the series?
I see 17 movies and 11 books. But it also says I read 13 books and watched 63 movies. Do those numbers matter?

Think about the goal: we want to compare the total number of movies in the series to the total number of books. Does the fact that you've already read some books or watched some movies change how many actually exist in the series?
No, I guess not. The 13 and 63 are just about what I've done, not how many there are total. So I just need the 17 and 11.
Spot on. You've filtered out the extra information. Now that you have the two relevant totals, what mathematical operation should you use to find out how many 'more' movies there are than books?
That's the correct method. Go ahead and perform that calculation.
You have correctly identified the numbers and the operation needed for this problem. To be completely sure of your result, I recommend double-checking your subtraction one more time!
